questions.q: A company's cloud team is responsible for health and event monitoring, patch and release management, and incident response for production workloads, so that they keep meeting the uptime the business has agreed to. Which AWS CAF perspective covers these capabilities?
questions.hint: Think about who keeps workloads running day to day, not who oversees the cloud program.
questions.explanation: The Operations perspective covers observability, event and incident management, patching, release management and making sure services meet agreed levels. Governance is about orchestrating cloud initiatives, program and risk management, and cloud financial management, not running workloads.

questions.q: An auditor asks a company to show exactly how a particular security group was configured on a specific date last month. The company also wants a custom rule that continuously flags any security group that allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0. Which service meets both needs?
questions.hint: You need a configuration history over time plus rules that you can define yourself.
questions.explanation: AWS Config records a configuration timeline for each resource and evaluates resources continuously against managed or custom Config rules. Trusted Advisor runs a fixed set of best-practice checks and gives recommendations, but it keeps no configuration history and doesn't support custom compliance rules.

questions.q: A loan application process must run a credit-check function, then branch to automatic approval or to a manual review that can take several days, retry failed calls automatically, and let staff see which step each application has reached. Which service should coordinate this process?
questions.hint: You need a service that keeps track of state, sequence and branches across many steps.
questions.explanation: AWS Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows as state machines, with branching, retries, long waits (including human approval) and a visual history of each execution. Amazon SNS only fans out messages to subscribers. It doesn't track state, enforce order or handle branching.

questions.q: A bank keeps its core transaction system in its own data center for regulatory reasons, but runs its customer-facing website and analytics on AWS, with the two environments connected over a VPN. Which cloud deployment model does this describe?
questions.hint: Some workloads are in the bank's own facility and some are in AWS, and the two are connected.
questions.explanation: A hybrid deployment connects on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources so that workloads can run in both. An all-in cloud deployment would run everything on AWS, and private cloud would keep everything on premises.

questions.q: Unwanted traffic from a known IP address range is hitting every instance in one subnet. The company wants a single rule that blocks that range for the whole subnet while all other traffic is still allowed. Which VPC feature should it use?
questions.hint: One of these filters at the subnet boundary and supports both allow and deny rules.
questions.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless firewalls at the subnet level that support explicit deny rules, so they can block a specific IP range. Security groups work at the instance (ENI) level and only support allow rules, so they can't deny one range.

questions.q: A company runs its application on Amazon EC2 instances. Which TWO tasks are the customer's responsibility under the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Securing network cabling in the data centers
questions.hint: EC2 is infrastructure as a service: AWS stops at the virtualization layer.
questions.explanation: With EC2, the customer manages everything from the guest OS up, including patching and firewall settings like security groups. The hypervisor, physical hardware and data center facilities are security 'of' the cloud, which is AWS's responsibility.

questions.q: An insurance company receives thousands of scanned claim forms every day. It wants to automatically extract printed and handwritten text, key-value form fields and tables from them, without building ML models. Which service fits?
questions.hint: The input is scanned documents, and the output needs to keep the structure of forms and tables.
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract extracts text, handwriting, form fields and tables from scanned documents. Rekognition analyzes images and video (objects, faces, simple text in scenes) but doesn't extract document structure, and Comprehend analyzes the meaning of text that has already been extracted.

questions.q: A data team wants a serverless service that uses crawlers to discover the schema of data in Amazon S3, stores it in a central data catalog, and runs jobs that transform and load the data, all without managing clusters. Which service should it use?
questions.hint: Look for the serverless ETL service that comes with a data catalog.
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration (ETL) service with crawlers and the Glue Data Catalog. Amazon EMR runs big-data frameworks such as Spark on clusters that you configure, and Athena queries data but doesn't crawl or transform it (Athena actually uses the Glue Data Catalog).

questions.q: A company wants to buy a preconfigured third-party firewall appliance and a monitoring tool that are ready to run on AWS, with the software charges showing up on its regular AWS bill. Where should it get them?
questions.hint: It's a digital catalog of software from independent vendors.
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated catalog of third-party software, data and services that you can deploy on AWS, with charges billed through your AWS account. AWS Service Catalog lets an organization publish its own approved products internally, but it doesn't sell third-party software.

questions.q: A FinOps team needs the most detailed billing data available: individual line items for each resource at hourly granularity, including cost allocation tags and Savings Plans details, delivered to an S3 bucket so that it can analyze them with Athena. Which option provides this?
questions.hint: The team wants raw, granular data files, not charts or alerts.
questions.explanation: The AWS Cost and Usage Report (now delivered through AWS Data Exports as CUR 2.0) is the most comprehensive billing dataset, with hourly, resource-level line items delivered to S3. Cost Explorer gives visual, aggregated views and forecasts but doesn't deliver full line-item files to S3.
